newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta exchange sees record turnover.
newsitem.headline: Malta exchange sees record turnover.

text.p: Turnover soared to new heights at the once-weekly trading session of the Malta stock exchange on Wednesday, fuelled by heavy selling of low-yield government bonds ahead of new bond issues having a higher coupon.
There were 233 deals on Wednesday, the highest ever, with turnover reaching just under 4.2 million Malta pounds ($10.97 million) pushing the aggregate turnover this year past 47 million pounds.
The previous highest was 46.2 million in 1995, which included 14 million in the Bank of Valletta share offer.

Business in equities on Wednesday reached just under 170,000 pounds, with 112,342 shares changing hands. Of these, 45,720 were Bank of Valletta shares traded in 42 deals at an average price of 126 cents, up two mils. There were 34 deals in Mid-Med Bank with 47,650 shares traded for an average 154.7 cents, down three mils.
There was one deal in Middle Sea Insurance with 2,626 shares sold for 122 cents, unchanged.
In Lombard Bank Malta 12,400 shares changed hands for an average 142.8 cents per share, down two mils since last traded two weeks ago.

In Simonds Farsons Cisk, 2,446 of the 8.5 percent preference shares 1996/99 were sold for 98 cents per share in one deal. Another 1,500 six percent preference shares 2001/3 were sold for an average 10 pounds each.

But the bulk of trading was in government bonds, where turnover reached just under four million pounds. Dealing was in 30 different issues, but mainly concentrated in the six percent MGS 1998, the 6.35 percent MGS 1998 (V) and the 6.35 percent MGS 1998 (VI).

The Malta government on Monday offered three bond issues with a coupon of 6.75 percent (three years), 7.25 percent (eight years) and 7.8 percent (15 years). The offers close on May 24, but could be closed earlier if over-subscribed.

In the corporate bond market, there were four deals in Mid- Med Bank 7.25 percent unsecured loan stock 2005, two deals in 6.5 percent Gasan bonds 1998/99 and one deal in 8.25 percent Suncrest Bonds 2005/7 amounting to 98,789 pounds; 1,186.80 Malta pounds and 1,000 pounds respectively. ($1 = 0.38 cents)
